title: searxng values
description: Values schema for the searxng chart (issue #68). additionalProperties is false on every chart-owned object level, so a key the chart does not read is rejected at render time instead of being silently ignored. Objects that go verbatim into the Kubernetes pod spec (probes, security contexts, global, free-form annotations) stay open, and so does settings.extra - its schema belongs to SearXNG, not to this chart. The schema ADDS to the required() calls in the templates, it does not replace them.

global.description: Helm's conventional cross-chart values. Unused by this chart, kept open so an umbrella install cannot break on it.

searxngSecretRef.description: op:// item path carrying a "secret-key" field. Required by the template - SearXNG exits 1 when server.secret_key is still the upstream placeholder.

valkeySecretRef.description: op:// item path carrying a "valkey-url" field for an external Valkey/Redis. Optional; only meaningful with settings.limiter: true.

settings.description: The chart-owned part of /etc/searxng/settings.yml. May be null / empty: the chart then falls back to its own defaults (issue #99) instead of rendering an instance with an empty name and no image proxy.

safeSearch.description: search.safe_search - 0 off, 1 moderate, 2 strict. Constrained because SearXNG accepts nothing else and a typo here would otherwise reach the app as a config error at start.

autocomplete.description: search.autocomplete - the suggestion backend, or the empty string to disable suggestions. Not enumerated: the list of backends is upstream's and grows.

limiter.description: server.limiter - the bot detection. Needs an external Valkey (secrets.valkeySecretRef) to do anything.

extra.description: Free-form SearXNG settings, merged over the block the keys above build and rendered verbatim into settings.yml. Deliberately open: the schema here is SearXNG's, and restricting it would only reject keys the upstream has not invented yet.

enabled.description: Gates the Ingress template only. ingress.domain is read a second time in the Deployment (SEARXNG_BASE_URL) and keeps its own required() there, so switching the Ingress off frees clusterIssuer but NOT domain.

annotations.description: Extra Ingress annotations, merged with the cert-manager annotation the chart always sets. Free-form keys by nature, so this object stays open.

resources.description: May be null / empty: the chart then falls back to its default requests and computed limits (issue #99) instead of rendering a container without resource accounting.

resourceList.description: Both spellings of the ephemeral-storage key are accepted because the resources helper normalizes camelCase to the Kubernetes key.

securityContext.description: May be null / empty at any level: the chart then falls back to its hardening defaults (issue #99) instead of rendering an unhardened workload. Those fallbacks reproduce THIS chart's uid/gid 977, not the repo's generic numbers.

pod.description: Merged onto the chart's pod hardening defaults and rendered as the pod's securityContext; kept open because the chart does not interpret the individual fields.

container.description: Merged onto the chart's container hardening defaults and rendered as the container's securityContext; kept open because the chart does not interpret the individual fields.

probe.description: Merged onto the chart's probe defaults and rendered as a container probe; kept open because the chart does not interpret the individual fields. May be null / empty, which means the defaults apply (issue #99) rather than the probe disappearing. The chart's defaults carry the probe's context - the /healthz path and the "http" port name - not just its timings.
